newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rice export prices firm on low stocks.
newsitem.headline: Indian rice export prices firm on low stocks.

text.p: Indian rice export prices hardened during the past week due to good export demand and lower domestic availability, traders said on Thursday.
"Prices are firming up due to low availability," Mulraj Tanna, a leading Bombay foodgrains exporter, told Reuters.
Prem Garg, a leading New Delhi foodgrains exporter, said: "Lot of demand is there for five percent broken, 100 pct broken and parboiled varieties."
Traders said five percent broken non-basmati was quoted at $315 per tonne fob, 10 percent at $300, 15 percent at $275-285 and 25 percent at $255-265 per tonne.
Indian parboiled rice for exports was quoted at about $270-$280 per tonne fob, traders said.
Demand for 100 percent broken grades was gradually picking up, mainly from African countries. It was quoted at $180 per tonne fob.
"About two or three vessels with 100 percent broken grades have been shipped in the last week," Tanna said.
Garg said demand for the five percent broken variety was mainly from the Commonwealth of Independent States and Middle East countries.
Traders said India exported about two million tonnes of non-basmati rice in 1996/97 (April-March).
"Exports are low this year and rightly so because domestic prices are high," Tanna said. India exported a record 5.5 million tonnes of rice in 1995/96.
"But basmati exports are doing well," Tanna said. Traders said India exported about 450,000 tonne of basmati in 1996/97.
Tanna said the government's decision to allow free imports of coarse rice and rice with more than 50 percent broken content was a "good move" as it would help stabilise domestic prices.
Traders said sowing for the next rice crop would begin in two weeks.
